summary: Court cases were opened on Oct. 30 against all three people arrested in the Fairbanks area overnight — two near Nenana and one in Fairbanks — and against a Fairbanks woman arrested for drunk driving before dawn on Oct. 30; five criminal cases were opened inside the area in all. The Fairbanks case against Daniel Zachary Schwietert, whose robbery charge was amended to a misdemeanor on Oct. 16, was disposed at a change-of-plea hearing on Oct. 30. A woman is charged with assault and two counts of assault when a child is present after a North Pole domestic disturbance on Oct. 28, and a Wiseman man is charged with drunk driving after a rollover at Delta Junction on Oct. 26. The Alaska Court System's weekly report of charges filed, covering Oct. 23 to Oct. 29, lists 48 cases at the four courthouses in the area — but 11 case numbers the Fairbanks court opened on Oct. 28 are absent from it for the second week running, so the report's count is lower than the number of cases opened in its own window, and the five cases opened on Oct. 30 fall outside it. The court's companion report of cases closed has still not been updated since Oct. 26.

entries.title: Assault charge: Emily Agnes Vance
body: Emily Agnes Vance, 40, of Nenana, is charged with assault in the fourth degree — recklessly injuring someone — a Class A misdemeanor, and criminal mischief in the fifth degree — damaging property worth less than $250 — a Class B misdemeanor. Both counts are recorded in the court file as domestic violence related. Near 2nd Street, Nenana, Oct. 29 at about 5:18 p.m.; Alaska State Troopers.
Troopers say they responded to a report of an assault in Nenana and that she entered a residence, caused damage to the front door and assaulted a person there.

Case 4NE-26-00107CR, opened Oct. 30. She was arraigned Oct. 30 and a $750 cash bond is recorded posted the same day; troopers had said she was held without bail. A rural calendar call is set for Dec. 15 at the Nenana courthouse.

entries.title: Driving with a revoked license: Michael Glen Latham
body: Michael Glen Latham, 56, of Willow, is charged with driving while his license was canceled, revoked or suspended for a criminal offense — driving after the state has withdrawn the driving privilege — a Class A misdemeanor, and with having no motor vehicle liability insurance, an unclassified misdemeanor. Mile 320 of the Parks Highway near Nenana, Oct. 29 at 8:36 p.m.; Alaska State Troopers.

Troopers say they stopped a 2001 Dodge pickup for several moving and equipment violations, including almost driving off the road in a construction zone, and found the driver had an outstanding warrant for a parole violation. He was remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center on the warrant and the new charges.
Case 4NE-26-00108CR, opened Oct. 30. He was arraigned Oct. 30; a rural calendar call is set for Dec. 15 at the Nenana courthouse.

entries.title: Assault charge: Maya Jade Newman
body: Maya Jade Newman, 25, is charged with assault in the fourth degree — causing fear of injury — a Class A misdemeanor, and unlawful contact in the second degree while charged with a Class A misdemeanor or felony offense, a Class B misdemeanor. Both counts are recorded in the court file as domestic violence related. 1500 block of Denali Way, Fairbanks, Oct. 29 at 5:32 p.m.; Fairbanks Police.
Police case 26003311. The police bulletin recorded both charges as misdemeanors without stating a class.
Case 4FA-26-02199CR, opened Oct. 30. She was arraigned Oct. 30 and a public defender was appointed; a pre-trial conference is set for Dec. 24 and a trial week beginning Jan. 4, 2027.

entries.title: DUI arrest: Janet Pulido
body: Janet Pulido, 25, was arrested on charges of driving under the influence and refusal to submit to a chemical test. Mitchell Expressway, Fairbanks, Oct. 30 at about 4:34 a.m.; Alaska State Troopers.

Troopers say they stopped her vehicle for excessive speed and that the investigation showed she was driving under the influence of an impairing substance. She was remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.
Case 4FA-26-02197CR was opened the same day; the court file does not yet state a charge or a charge class. An arraignment is set for Nov. 6. She is arrested, not convicted.

entries.title: Failure to file an accident report: Anthony Joseph Thelen
body: Anthony Joseph Thelen is charged with failing to file a report of a traffic accident within ten days, an unclassified misdemeanor.

The offense is recorded as having taken place at Fairbanks on Sep. 24. Case 4FA-26-02198CR, opened Oct. 30 on a summons issued to the Alaska State Troopers at Fairbanks. No hearing has been set. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Assault and assault-when-child-present charges: Maia Mae Hannum
body: Maia Mae Hannum, 32, of North Pole, is charged with assault in the fourth degree — recklessly injuring someone — and two counts of assault when a child is present. All three counts are Class A misdemeanors and all three are recorded in the court file as domestic violence related. North Pole, Oct. 28 at about 6 a.m.; Alaska State Troopers.

Troopers say they responded to a report of a domestic disturbance at a North Pole residence and determined that a household member had been assaulted in the presence of two children. The trooper release does not name anyone. She was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.
Case 4FA-26-02179CR. She was arraigned Oct. 28; a bail hearing on Oct. 30 was continued to Nov. 6. A pre-trial conference is set for Dec. 24 and a trial week beginning Jan. 4, 2027.

entries.title: DUI and criminal mischief charges: Christian Von Kirchner
body: Christian Von Kirchner, 34, of Wiseman, is charged with driving under the influence with a blood alcohol content of .08 percent or more, a Class A misdemeanor, and criminal mischief in the fifth degree — damaging property worth less than $250 — a Class B misdemeanor. Delta Junction, Oct. 26; Alaska State Troopers.

According to the News-Miner public safety report, citing court documents, troopers responded to a single-vehicle rollover at the Alaska Highway and South Clearwater Avenue, and Kirchner said he had been driving the Subaru found in a ditch. The report says he appeared intoxicated and failed sobriety tests, that the trooper found two opened bottles of alcohol in the vehicle, that a breath sample measured 0.202, and that he damaged two sets of handcuffs before being taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.

Case 4DJ-26-00066CR. He was arraigned Oct. 27 and $500 bail was posted Oct. 29; a rural calendar call is set for Dec. 15 at the Delta Junction courthouse. A separate trooper citation for basic speed, case 4DJ-26-00623MO, was filed Oct. 29 for the same date, carrying a $90 fine and a $20 surcharge.

entries.title: Criminal trespass arrest: Jerome Benjamin Semaken
body: Jerome Benjamin Semaken, 42, was arrested on a charge of criminal trespass in the second degree — entering or remaining on premises unlawfully — recorded by police as a misdemeanor. 100 block of Lacey Street, Fairbanks, Oct. 28 at noon; Fairbanks Police.
Police case 26002099. No court case had been opened in the matter as of the evening of Oct. 30. He is arrested, not convicted.

entries.title: Case disposed: Daniel Zachary Schwietert
body: The Fairbanks case against Daniel Zachary Schwietert, arising from an Oct. 12 incident at a Fairbanks sporting goods store, was disposed at a change-of-plea hearing on Oct. 30 before Judge Ben Seekins. The court file records a criminal judgment or disposition order entered the same day; it does not state the plea, the finding or the sentence.

The charge at disposition was attempted theft in the third degree — taking property worth $250 to $749 — a Class B misdemeanor. The file records an original charge of robbery in the first degree, a Class A felony, and the amended charge entered on Oct. 16.
Troopers said at the time that they were called to Beaver Sports in Fairbanks at 1:46 p.m. on Oct. 12 for a reported robbery and arrested him. Case 4FA-26-02078CR.

entries.title: Drug indictment: Rayann Marlisa Carroll
body: Rayann Marlisa Carroll has been indicted on a charge of misconduct involving a controlled substance in the second degree — making or delivering a schedule IA controlled substance — a Class A felony, punishable by up to 20 years.

A Fairbanks grand jury returned the indictment on Oct. 29 and the case was transferred to the Superior Court the same day. The charge was first filed on Oct. 21 and the offense is recorded as having taken place at Fairbanks on Oct. 20.

Case 4FA-26-02128CR; superior court arraignment Nov. 4 before Judge Thomas Temple, with an omnibus hearing Dec. 17 and a trial week beginning Jan. 4, 2027. An indictment is a grand jury's finding that a case may go forward and is not a conviction.

entries.title: Criminal mischief charge: Dalton Curtis Wayne Benefield
body: Dalton Curtis Wayne Benefield is charged with criminal mischief in the fourth degree — damaging property worth $250 to $749 — a Class A misdemeanor, recorded in the court file as domestic violence related.

Troopers say they responded to a disturbance on Homer Drive in North Pole on Oct. 28, found extensive damage to the residence they attribute to Benefield, estimated the damage at more than $750, and arrested him on a charge of criminal mischief in the third degree. The charge filed in court is one degree lower.
Case 4FA-26-02178CR; pre-trial conference Dec. 24 and a trial week beginning Jan. 4, 2027.

entries.title: Driving with a suspended license: James Patrick Carpentino
body: James Patrick Carpentino, 48, of North Pole, is charged with driving with a license in violation of limits with a previous conviction, a Class A misdemeanor. The charge was entered on the court file on Oct. 29.

Troopers say they stopped him at about 5:09 p.m. on Oct. 27 for a moving violation and found he was driving while his license was suspended for a criminal offense, with a prior conviction for the same offense in the past 10 years. He was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.
Case 4FA-26-02176CR; arraignment Nov. 3.

entries.title: Court's weekly list of closed cases has not been updated since Oct. 26
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly report of criminal cases disposed, which lists cases closed statewide, still carries the data of Oct. 26 and has not been refreshed on any of the four mornings since.

No Interior case closed after Oct. 26 can be read from it; the Fairbanks case disposed on Oct. 30 and reported above was taken from the court file itself. The court's companion report of criminal charges filed has been refreshed each morning over the same period, most recently on Oct. 30.
